body:
`helper.get_book_cover_with_uuid` (cps/helper.py) and `helper.get_kobo_cover_source_path`
resolve the book with `calibre_db.get_book_by_uuid`, which applies NO filter (cps/db.py) —
unlike the numbered `/cover/<id>` route, which goes through `get_filtered_book` and therefore
`common_filters`. `cps/kobo.py`'s cover handler uses the same raw lookup.

A policy-aware alternative already exists and is used elsewhere:
`get_book_by_uuid_for_kobo(..., enforce_policy=True)` (cps/db.py).

So a Kobo cover request naming another user's restricted book's UUID is answered from that
book rather than refused. Pre-existing; found by an adversarial review of PR #1739 (which
asked explicitly whether its new cache policy could attach to "a different user's book" — the
caching change does not reach this path, but the underlying lookup does).

Smallest fix: use the policy-aware lookup in both UUID cover helpers.
title: Kobo cover lookup by UUID bypasses per-user visibility filtering

resolution.note: Fixed by #1947 (My Library) as a side effect of routing every book lookup through common_filters. All three sites the finding names now use get_book_by_uuid_for_kobo(..., enforce_policy=True): helper.get_book_cover_with_uuid, helper.get_kobo_cover_source_path, and the kobo.py cover handler. VERIFIED on main 1b5417a2a by reading each call site, not by trusting the merge. The remaining enforce_policy=False sites are the device-trailing ownership/state endpoints, which are deliberately unfiltered per notes/KOBO-B4-COMMON-FILTERS-POLICY.md so a device can always clean up books it already holds. IT WAS FIXED BUT UNGUARDED: TestNoLegacyBypass audited cps/kobo.py only, and both cover helpers live in cps/helper.py, so reverting either line reintroduced the bug with a fully green suite. Closed together with a regression guard (test_the_two_kobo_cover_helpers_enforce_policy), mutation-tested two ways - reverting helper A to the raw lookup, and flipping helper B to enforce_policy=False - both red.
